summary: A pair of small wooden range towers at Northport that guide vessels toward Alberton Harbour and Cascumpec Bay, moved and raised several times since the 1880s.

access.note: Rear tower on community-owned land in a residential area; operating aid to navigation.

events.note: Heritage record: built 1885 by James Keefe as open-frame front range light
3.3 m added to the original construction
Old front tower moved to become the rear light when a new front lighthouse was built
Heritage lighthouse under the Heritage Lighthouses Protection Act

keepers.name: Wm. Champion
keepers.note: Appointed 25 Oct 1897 per 1904 keepers statement, p. 163; row matched by position, confirmed on page image

evidence.supports: built 1885 by James Keefe, front range, open frame
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1885 by builder James Keefe, the Northport Rear Range Lighthouse was based on a Department of Marine and Fisheries design.
It was enclosed in 1903. In 1962, when a new lighthouse was built, this lighthouse, formerly the Front Range Lighthouse was moved to become the back or Rear Range Light.
Extra height was added to the original construction in 1887 (3.3 metres) and an additional 1.8 metres was added in 1970.
The original back or rear range lighthouse was sold, moved nearby, and refurbished as a private residence.
John Mountain (1885-1897), B. Mountain (1912-1914), W.A. Smith (1914-1923, and possibly longer), Joseph Perry (1926-1948), Lemuel Arsenault (1948), and James Andrew Gallant (1948-1961).
The community has assumed ownership of the lighthouse which was designated in 2015 under the federal Heritage Lighthouses Protection Act.
It has been moved four times and elevated twice to suit the needs of the changing route through the channel into Alberton Harbour and Cascumpec Bay.
Set in a residential area on a flat grassy parcel of land about 20 metres from the shoreline, the lighthouse is highly visible from the water.
Its accessible location contributes to its familiarity and facilitates its appreciation by the public.

evidence.supports: channel change and Northport red lights
evidence.quote: In consequence of a serious change in the position of the channel over the bar at the mouth of this harbour, caused by last winter's storms

They should keep this range in one until the red lights at North- port are in one, but care must be taken not to overrun the alignment of the red lights, as the intersection of the two alignments is very close to the shoal off Kildare point.
Xorthport. — The towers from which the range lights are shown have been enclosed and painted white.
White pyramid tower with red vertical stripe.
Square skeleton tower, white rectangular daymark with red vertical stripe.

notes_for_editor: Heritage register says built 1885 (front tower, builder James Keefe), John Mountain keeper to 1897; the 1904 keepers statement shows Wm. Champion appointed 25 Oct 1897 at Northport Range (row position, verified on the page image, printed p.163); no real conflict. Wikipedia/Wikidata-derived records say 1897 and 1962 first lit, which the register explains as the old front tower becoming the rear. Record lists two NRHP-style register entries (20730 statement, 20884 description). Keeper names between 1897 and 1912 not found;  Fiscal 1903 report page 71 taken from printed page head in OCR. Record characteristic Iso G 1s differs from CCG Iso G 4s.
